candidate.name: David Voyles
candidate.headline: Senior Technical Program Manager · Publishing Pipelines · AI Telemetry

summary.text: Senior technical program manager in product delivery, taking platform and AI capabilities from design to GA and retention: entitlements, publishing pipelines, and live evals on production traffic. Partners with engineering on API contracts that surface in systems customers already use, and kept 8 partner systems on their existing tools through ownership transfers.

jobs.title: Agentic Platforms
bullets: Risk management for the running stack: routing and tool-call changes gated by live evals on every request plus CI replay, so it fails closed before a bad change lands.
Run an agentic workflow of personalized agents with A/B testing of local and cloud models, plus a self-improvement loop (167 skills, 57 commands, live evals); operated, never authored.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Partner Center / Xbox
bullets: Led release management for Fast Game Package Publishing inside Partner Center (the existing publisher workflow), cutting SLA 12 hours to 30 minutes (24x); P90 under 10 minutes; production-traffic shadowing with zero release risk.

Designed Game Reparenting Validate / Execute Reparent APIs for dependency management across 8 partner systems, which kept their existing tools through ownership transfers; Saga compensating transactions; 100% data fidelity, zero rollbacks.

Orchestrated an internal AI telemetry pipeline for data analytics across 74 Azure DevOps queries for 14 PM teams, putting hygiene, trends, and alerts into the work-tracking system they already lived in.
Led change management for the Xbox 360 catalog modernization of 30,000+ items, protecting $50M annual revenue and $15M annual profit with zero storefront downtime.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
bullets: Stakeholder management as a senior IC: delivered with stakeholders in the room, then shipped the APIs and pipelines those teams kept.
Translated enterprise account workflows into platform capabilities those product teams retained after CSE left.
